_readme: The W1 labelled evaluation set: 63 drafts with a known verdict (the spec asked for 50), half written to be caught and half written to be let through. It exists for two jobs. (1) It is the evidence that the claim-level verifier is BOTH sound and usable: the false-negative rate over the `fail` cases must be zero, because a fabricated claim that passes is the failure this whole product exists to prevent, and the false-positive rate over the `pass` cases must stay low enough that a `held` draft still means something to the reviewer. (2) It is the permanent regression suite for every later change to the verifier, the lexicon, or the drafting prompt: a prompt edit that starts producing copy this set marks as legitimate, or a lexicon edit that starts admitting fabrication, shows up here as a number rather than as a surprise in the client's review queue. Run it with tests/test_verify.py. The corpus below is copied verbatim from the Phase 1 seed fixtures (tests/fixtures/company/*.json), INCLUDING the '[date] ' prefix that the company adapter prepends to fact content, so the evidence has exactly the shape production stores in research_cache. It is copied rather than imported on purpose: those fixtures belong to integrations-engineer and are free to change, and a regression suite whose labels can move underneath it is not a regression suite.

cases.why: The headline adversarial case for speaker-awareness. First-person framing around a claim about THEM. The sentence says 'I saw', but what it asserts is the recipient's headcount, and 40 is in no fact. Second person anywhere in the span makes the whole span checkable.
cases.subject: Your support team
cases.body: Tom, I saw you scaled to 40 support reps this year. I work with teams at exactly that size.

cases.why: No second person, no company name, first person present: on pronouns alone this reads as the sender talking about the sender. It is not. 'We think' introduces a proposition about the recipient, which is why a cognition verb disqualifies a span from the sender-voice exemption no matter what pronouns surround it.
cases.subject: Notes from the offsite
cases.body: Tom, thanks for the offsite write-up. We think headcount doubled last quarter, and that is usually when a clinic question starts getting lost.

cases.why: The subtle version of the same smuggle: drop 'you' entirely and let 'the support team' do the referring. Only the reporting verb stands between this and an exempt span, and it holds. A fabricated 40 is a fabricated 40 in any grammatical person.
cases.subject: Support triage
cases.body: Tom, I noticed the support team just passed 40 people. Happy to share what that usually breaks first.

cases.why: A job title is a claim about the recipient's org chart wherever it appears, so job titles are NOT exempted by speaker at all. Northwind posted a Revenue Operations Manager; a Head of Revenue Operations search is a different company's story, and putting it in the sender's own sentence does not change that.
cases.subject: Revenue operations
cases.body: Dana, I spend most of my week with companies hiring a Head of Revenue Operations, and I wanted to reach out while it is live.

cases.why: Proper nouns are not exempted by speaker either. A named third party in the sender's own sentence is still a name in a cold email that traces to nothing, and 'if it is right by accident' is not a standard this control works to.
cases.subject: Routing work
cases.body: Dana, I can share what we built with Brightpath Freight when they untangled lead routing.
